extracted.intended_audience: naval managers, government contracting officials, public administration researchers, and policymakers concerned with OMB Circular A-76 implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Assess implementation outcomes of OMB Circular A-76 contracting out in the U.S. Navy, focusing on post-award costs, underestimated or unaccounted costs, and administrative/policy shortcomings. The thesis analyzes 14 West Coast activities that contracted out food service and storage/warehousing operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of pre-award cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The accuracy of pre-award cost estimates used to estimate post-award program savings in operations that are contracted out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis examines whether pre-award estimates accurately predict post-award savings; it focuses on costs that are underestimated or omitted in the cost comparison process across 14 contracted activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and accounting of post-award costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether post-award costs are identified and properly accounted for in the cost comparison and contracting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should look for costs that were underestimated or not accounted for after award; the study identifies such costs in food service and storage/warehousing contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award guidance and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence and adequacy of post-award guidance and policy governing contracted operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study highlights a need for post-award guidance and policy — assess whether clear policies exist for managing post-award issues and cost tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimant guidance at the field level
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and sufficiency of guidance provided to claimants at the field (operational) level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis notes the need for increased claimant guidance at the field level; reviewers should check for training, instructions, and local support for claimants handling contracted functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of cost accounting systems and post-award program controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether cost accounting systems and post-award program controls are adequate to track and manage costs after contracting out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page reports an absence of an adequate cost accounting system and post-award program controls; assessments should verify existence, granularity, and reliability of accounting and control mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration staffing levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficiency of contract administration staffing to manage and oversee contracted operations post-award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study identifies a need for increased contract administration staffing; evaluate staffing levels, workloads, and capability to monitor contractor performance and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget flexibility for activities that have contracted out
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether activities that contracted out retain necessary budget flexibility to respond to post-award needs and changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis points to a problem with budget flexibility at activities that have contracted out; reviewers should examine budget structures and constraints affecting contracted operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and definition of performance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The precision and adequacy of performance definitions used in contracts and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing problems with performance definition were identified; evaluators should inspect statements of work, performance standards, and measurement criteria for ambiguity or gaps.
